title: The forest with him
hookLine: Rama tells Sita to stay home while he goes into exile, and she argues, and wins
carry: married partners walk one dharma, side by side
tomorrow: what can a blade of grass do?
last: SITA IS EARTH'S DAUGHTER, AND THE EARTH IS MOTHER.

lines: I WILL WALK AHEAD OF YOU.
cards: I will walk ahead of you. That, in paraphrase, is Sita's answer when Rama comes to tell her he's been sent into the forest, and that she should stay behind. The crown he was promised has been taken away.
He's leaving soon. He has a careful speech ready about how she should live in Ayodhya while he's gone: honor his parents, don't praise him in front of the new heir. Sita doesn't take the speech.
She takes the floor. Today: the argument in Valmiki's second book, where Sita's own words decide where she goes.

teach.h: A WIFE SHARES HER HUSBAND'S LOT
teach.b: She starts with a reason. A father, a mother, a brother, a son, she says, each lives by their own lot. A wife shares her husband's.
If he is sent to the forest, so is she. Then she gets practical.
I'll go first, and tread down the thorns and the sharp grass on the path. The forest with you is better to me than any palace without you. Rama tries again.

He describes the forest honestly: wild animals, cold, hunger, sleeping on the ground. And here the text lets Sita get angry. In paraphrase: what was my father thinking, she asks, when he took you as a son-in-law?
Did he think you were a man, when you're a woman in a man's form? It's a sharp line, and Valmiki keeps it. Then she weeps, and holds him, and Rama gives way.
Come, he says. Her argument rests on a Hindu teaching about marriage.
A wife is called sahadharmini: one who walks in dharma together with her husband.

It's why, at a Hindu wedding, the couple take seven steps together before the sacred fire, and why many rites are done by the two side by side. Sita takes that teaching and turns it into an argument Rama can't refuse.
Some readers hear devotion here first; others hear a woman choosing her own road against the man trying to choose it for her. The text holds both, and gives her the words either way.
The thorns she promises to tread down are hers to tread.

how: Sita's choice to follow Rama into exile is retold in Ramayana recitations and Ram Lila performances; at Hindu weddings the couple take seven steps together, the saptapadi, as partners in dharma.

games.q: you're Sita. Rama has lost the crown and is going into the forest. he asks you to stay in the palace and look after his parents. what do you do?
o: argue, and insist on going with him.
go back to your father's house.
games.why: she argues from the dharma a wife shares with her husband, from love and finally in anger; then she weeps, and Rama says: come.

practice: Bring to mind one road ahead of you, a hard conversation, a move, a long week, and let someone you love come to mind alongside it.
Ask quietly whether there's a thorn on that path you could tread down first, for them, and don't plan it; just breathe with whatever shows itself. If you pray, you can hold that person before God.

wordCard.voice: Sita. In Valmiki's second book, she refuses to stay behind, argues with Rama, and walks into exile at his side. Today's word.
